expectations.text: Lists the all-hazards, 10-measure minimum set — policies on risk analysis, incident handling, business continuity/backup/DR/crisis management, supply chain security, secure development/vulnerability handling, effectiveness testing, cyber hygiene/training, cryptography policies, HR/access control/asset management, and MFA/secured communications
expectations.evidence: based on an 'all-hazards approach'... enumerates all ten Article 21(2) domains from risk analysis through MFA/secured communications

expectations.text: Emphasises supply chain security including direct supplier relationships as an explicit measure
expectations.evidence: Supply chain security, including security-related aspects concerning relationships between each entity and its direct suppliers or service providers

expectations.text: Notes proportionality: measures appropriate to the risks, entity size, and societal impact
expectations.evidence: Proportionality is assessed against your degree of risk exposure, size, likelihood/severity of incidents, and cost of implementation

expectations.text: Mentions the effectiveness-assessment obligation (policies and procedures to assess whether measures work)
expectations.evidence: Policies and procedures to assess the effectiveness of cybersecurity risk-management measures... actually test and measure whether your controls work

expectations.text: Frames ISO 27001 correctly if raised: strong implementation vehicle but not a safe harbor (registration, reporting timelines, governance duties sit outside certification)
expectations.evidence: this becomes a gap-mapping and documentation exercise... make sure Article 20 governance evidence (board approval, management training records) exists alongside — ISO framed as vehicle requiring gap work, not automatic compliance
